injected_faults.summary: A concurrency change at 15:55:00Z raised workers from 8 to 32 without enlarging the connection pool of 20, exhausting it from 15:58:10Z.
Independently, the flags.internal service token expired at 15:59:00Z and the worker fails closed without the flag, adding a second failure mode that the pool fix did not address.

required_facts.claim: Settlement failures reached 0.61 against an objective of 0.02.
The database connection pool of 20 was exhausted from 15:58:10Z with pool_timeout errors.
The flags.internal service token expired at 15:59:00Z and calls returned 401 invalid_token.
Worker concurrency was raised from 8 to 32 at 15:55:00Z while pool size stayed at 20.
Enlarging the pool at 17:20:15Z stopped pool_timeout errors but only reduced the failure ratio from 0.61 to 0.29.
Replacing the token at 18:12:10Z reduced the failure ratio from 0.29 to 0.004.
The failure-ratio series shows two distinct step changes, each aligned with a different remediation.

inference_only.claim: Attributing the incident to one fault is an inference and a wrong one.

contradicted_hypotheses.claim: Pool exhaustion alone explains the settlement failures.

required_open_questions.question: Why is pool size not derived from worker concurrency?
Which other service tokens are on manual renewal?
What settlement value was at risk?

rubric.adversarial_element: Two simultaneous root causes starting four minutes apart. A report naming one is incomplete rather than wrong, and the failure-ratio series showing two step changes is the mechanical tell. Scoring should reward a report whose hypotheses cover both faults.
rubric.misleading_correlation: deploy-5510 at 15:55 is causal for one fault and irrelevant to the other, so proximity supports a partial answer that feels complete.
rubric.evidence_gap: No record states the settlement value at risk.
